newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking developed ahead of the long holiday weekend and pressured CME lumber futures after values posted initial gains, traders said.
Lumber closed $2.90 per thousand board feet lower to $0.90 higher with May off most at $378.50 per tbf and July settled off $0.10 at $372.70 per tbf.

Profit taking developed shortly after the start with a lower bond market adding to weakness and offset a strong U.S. February existing home sales report and indications of a firmer tone to the cash lumber market, traders said.
Cash trade had been expected to be slow over the long holiday weekend, they said.

The National Association of Realtors said sales of existing U.S. homes rose 9.0 percent in February to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.26 million units. Economists had forecast February sales of 4.05 million units.

CME lumber futures will not trade Friday and both U.S. and Canadian cash markets will be closed Friday in observance of Good Friday ahead of the Easter holiday. Canada lumber markets will also be closed Monday in observance of Easter.
